To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the distribution of water vapor in the tropics is strongly constrained by thermodynamic considerations, that the dynamic component of water vapor is the dominant influence on interannual variability and decadal trends, that trends in water vapor are generally incoherence with trends in precipitation and that the distribution of the water vapor is not strongly constrained by thermodynamics. [2]

the spatial distribution of water vapor is strongly determined by the thermodynamic constraints and the spatial variability in water vapor is dominated by changes to the large-scale dynamics in the tropical region, especially associated with the ENSO.

the spatial distribution and temporal variability of tropical water vapor is strongly influenced by the large-scale dynamics and that the thermodynamic component of water vapor variability is an important factor in the determination of precipitation variability in the tropical oceans.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the spatial and temporal distribution of water vapor in the tropics.
the variability of water vapor over the tropics and the links to dynamics and radiative cooling via latent heating.
the variability in the tropospheric column integrated water vapor (CW) and its link with dynamics and precipitation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dynamics are more important than thermodynamics in the variability of CWV and precipitation in the tropics.
the dynamic component of water vapor variability is more important than the thermodynamic component in determining tropical variability in precipitation. [2]
the dynamic component of water vapor is a major factor influencing the variability of precipitation in the tropics. [2]
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
water vapor is a major component of the tropical climate system, with a strong dynamic component, and that the water vapor–precipitation relationship is complex. [2]
the thermodynamic component of CWV variability is a major factor for determining precipitation variability in some regions/ seasons, while it cancels its effect in some others.
the variability of water vapor in the tropics is primarily determined by the large-scale dynamics and is not well correlated with precipitation variability, except over the equatorial Atlantic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
water vapor variability is strongly influenced by dynamics in the tropics.
the spatial variability in CWV and its trends are strongly controlled by dynamics, while the variability in the precipitation is more thermodynamically controlled. [2]
thermodynamic changes in water vapor are not a major factor in explaining precipitation variability in the tropical regions analyzed.
